provenance.author: block writer B2 (Claude Opus 5.5, model-written)
notes: Frame: Mali reads three diary entries aloud to Arth (Ddoe = the river day of Penodau 9–10, Neithiwr = the kitchen night of Pennod 11, Heddiw = the stranger). Retelling by a character is the chapter's repetition engine (§6.2.3); Arth's competing version of the pike episode supplies the 'compare versions' beat.

Target handling (per the block plan): the productive core is Wnes i / Wnest ti + soft-mutated verb-noun, with es / des / ces i as the irregular short forms. Third-person past and Do / Naddo are not used (Pennod 13); past negatives are avoided. Past yes/no questions are answered with statements, never with Do / Naddo. Question-verb SM is exposed in Welaist ti …? (Cai) and Wnest ti …?; object SM after an inflected past is kept to three glossed instances (gwelais i benhwyad, gwelais i ddyn, ces i gawl).

The checker flags every mutated verb-noun after 'wnes i' as 'i + SM (Pennod 16)'; this is a false positive (the trigger is wnes i, taught here), but each first mutated verb-noun is glossed anyway (bysgota, weld, guddio, deimlo) because the mutation is new to the learner.

Remaining local-density warning (s096–s097): the five items (diwrnod, rhyfedd, ateb, gwych, wnest) are all this chapter's lexemes already met two or more times earlier in the chapter; the window straddles the end of the diary entry and Arth's reaction.
Lemma-validation warnings for pluen and blinedig concern planned lexemes (chapters.json); flagged for the fluent reviewer, not changed.
New form licensed in the delta: gwelaist ti (cy-gweld, 2sg preterite, for the question Welaist ti …?), because the -aist suffix is only registered from Pennod 13.

Codex review 2026-10-12, verdicts on the [?] questions: s044 already reads 'a wnes i' (the question quoted a superseded text); s045 speaker-labelled diary fragments accepted; s090 vocative 'Ferch' accepted (curt, fits the stranger); s030 'Dim eto' accepted (eto 'yet' recorded as cy-eto-s2 in the Pennod 11 delta); s124 objectless 'Wyt ti'n ofni?' accepted; s046 'gyda chen … ac asgell' correct; s073 object SM after ces/gwelais correct; s102 noun ateb accepted, lexical entry repaired (cy-ateb-s2, gender m, plural atebion).

Applied from the Codex review (2026-10-12): s021 'dw i'n cofio'r diwrnod ac yn ysgrifennu yn y llyfr' (no calque 'ysgrifennu'r diwrnod'; am is not available until 16) and the C.c1 model answer to match; s129 'Dyw'r gannwyll ddim yn llosgi nawr'; wedi ↔ ddoe table relabelled Dw i wedi … / Wnes i … · Es i … and A.a8 cue/hint no longer imply that heddiw or nawr selects wedi; 'weithiau' removed from the object-mutation row; A.a10 ag hint now says vowel sound; A.a1–a7 accept Gwnes i / Gwelais i variants and the supplied ddoe/neithiwr cue; C.c2 and C.c4 accept full sentences.
Recall pass 2026-10-18: recurrence added for cy-ph-dim-ond (Pennod 8) in s011 (Mali: 'Dim ond inc yw e'). No other changes.

Audit-fix pass 2026-10-19: cut the recall-pass ink-sniffing bolt-on (s009–s011, 'Dim ond inc yw e'); s012 now dips the quill in the ink (inc keeps three uses). The diary's unannounced 'Name: speech' lines (s045, s068, s090, s092, s132) now use tense-neutral meddai ('Wedyn, meddai Myrddin: …'; s092 'Wnes i ateb: …', which also makes ateb inferable before s099). Glosses: cofio glossed at its first use (s021), the cofio ↔ anghofio pair moved to anghofio's first use (s056); yn gyntaf (s042) no longer glossed with words not yet met, the 1 → 2 → 3 sequence now sits on yn olaf (s050); rhyfedd's opaque '? ! ?' replaced by 'Pwy? Pam? Beth?'; redundant Atishŵ gloss removed (declared incidental). s102 'Ateb yw e, ond …' removes the progressive/noun ambiguity. Cut s136 (a third 'Wedyn, wnes i …' in the Neithiwr entry) and dropped 'Yn gyntaf' from s085 so the third entry is not the same chain again. The tiredness drill after the climax is gone: s127 is now Mali's 'A fi hefyd' (she is afraid too); blinedig keeps three uses because s003 now opens 'Mae Mali'n flinedig, ond dyw hi ddim yn cysgu', which Arth's s015 echoes. s035 object question 'beth wyt ti'n guddio'. Pensa: B.b8 rewritten so only ofnadwy fits (rhyfedd no longer); C.c4 asks where Mali saw the stranger (s130 says the road is now empty); C.c2, A.a4, A.a5 accept further answers. Gramadeg: 'dim newid' replaced by n → n · a → a · ch → ch; the 'wedi ↔ ddoe' caption no longer keys the tense to a time word.

cover.alt: Night in the llys kitchen: Mali writes in a small book with a quill by candlelight while Dafi, sitting on the table, lights the candle with a tiny flame; Arth peeps round the door.
cover.art_brief: Llys kitchen at night (match place-cegin.png): dark timber, limewash, the clay oven glowing faintly, everything else in deep blue shadow. Mali (12, long dark braid, dark-blue dress, ink-stained fingers) sits at the end of the long table writing with a white goose quill in a small leather-bound book; a clay ink pot beside her. On the table Dafi (red dragon small enough to sit inside a wooden drinking cup; cream horns, tiny bat wings, big yellow eyes, spade-tipped tail) leans towards a short white candle in a clay holder and breathes a tiny flame onto the wick, which lights; warm light falls on Mali's face and the page (the page shows only blurry lines and a tiny sketch of a fish, no readable letters). In the inner doorway Arth (11, untidy brown hair with cowlick, oversized moss-green tunic, barefoot, sleepy) peeps in. Llys palette, candlelight. No text.

grammar.nodyn_en: Wnes i + verb-noun tells what you did: Wnes i weld 'I saw'. Ask Wnest ti …? 'Did you …?' or Beth wnest ti? The verb-noun softens (gweld → weld). Short forms: es i 'I went', des i 'I came', ces i 'I had'. Wedi = has happened; this past = happened then (ddoe).
